gate-flake.enabled.description: TX11 (D-070, docs/units/TX11/plan.md): after the known-base-defect step, a failing test of gate-flake.stages that the PR did not touch is re-run once at the same head; one that passes is attributed flake (recorded, shown, quarantined on its second sighting) and does not turn the PR red. Off is the rollback: no re-run, every failure stays the PR's.

gate-flake.never_excuse_touched.description: A failing test whose own file, covers manifest or declared covers the PR changed (defect_detect.touched) is not re-run and stays the PR's: a flaky test the PR wrote or changed is the PR's fault.

gate-flake.quarantine_after.description: test.flaked events for one test inside gate-flake.quarantine_window_s (this sighting included) after which the gate emits test.quarantined (quarantine.py). The quarantine changes no policy: the test is still listed and still blocks when it fails twice.

gate-flake.quarantine_window_s.description: Window, ending at the gate's clock, in which earlier test.flaked events of the same test count toward gate-flake.quarantine_after.

gate-flake.rerun_source.description: The source name the re-run passes to gate_test_cache.run.

gate-flake.rerun_store_prefix.description: Prefix of the throwaway cache directory the re-run uses, so it neither reads nor writes a gate_test_cache marker; deleted afterwards.

gate-flake.reruns.description: Re-runs of each failing test at the same head. Exactly one (T4/T8): a test that fails on it stays the PR's own; a second re-run would hide a real intermittent failure.

gate-flake.stages.description: Gate stages whose failing tests are re-run alone through gate_test_cache.run. A stage outside this list is never attributed flake.

gate-flake.subject_env.description: Environment variable gate-local exports with the checkout under test; the re-run runs there. Unset (a direct call outside gate-local): the tool checkout.
